title: Like, As, Is — Again
welcome_lead: Three of the biggest figures of speech.
meta_desc: KS3 English Language adventure on simile, metaphor and personification.
final_note: You can now spot simile, metaphor and personification at speed.

walkthroughs.body_html: 'The trees whispered' uses personification. Non-human things gain human action or feeling.
Literal = exact ('he is a doctor'). Figurative = image ('he is a rock'). Spot which mode the writer uses.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between descriptive and prescriptive approaches to language?
options: Descriptivists describe how language is actually used; prescriptivists rule on how language ought to be used — modern linguistics is descriptivist.
Descriptivists describe written language and prescriptivists describe spoken language.
Women and men have different vocal cords so speak differently.
Both terms mean the same — analysing language scientifically.

mcqs.q: Are claims that women use more 'tentative' language well-supported?
options: Women and men have different vocal cords so speak differently.
Early studies (Lakoff) made broad claims, but later research (e.g. Holmes, Cameron) shows context matters more than gender, and many supposed differences disappear with proper data.
Women always use more hedges and tag questions than men.
Both terms mean the same — analysing language scientifically.
RP is the correct way to speak English.
A prestige accent associated historically with public schools and the BBC — spoken by a small minority of Britons; it is an accent, not a dialect.
Both terms mean the same — analysing language scientifically.
RP is the accent everyone in southern England uses.
